title: Declare test dependencies in pyproject.toml
requirements: R1. `pyproject.toml` contains a `[project.optional-dependencies]` table with exactly one key, `test`, whose value is an array of exactly one string: a `pytest` requirement with a `>=` lower bound and no upper bound (`<`, `<=`, `==`, `~=` or a second clause after a comma must all be absent).
R2. `[project] dependencies` remains the literal empty array `dependencies = []` and no runtime requirement is added anywhere.

R3. `_build_backend.py` `_metadata()` emits the line `Provides-Extra: test` (exact extra name, no normalization drift) and, for each requirement declared under the `test` extra, one `Requires-Dist: <requirement>; extra == "test"` line, with the marker appended to the declared requirement string verbatim.

R4. The pytest requirement in the emitted metadata has exactly one source: the backend reads the `test` extra out of `pyproject.toml` at build time and must not contain a second literal of the pytest requirement (no `REQUIREMENT = "pytest..."` constant duplicating it).

R5. When `tomllib` cannot be imported (Python 3.9/3.10), the backend parses the extras from `pyproject.toml` with an in-tree parser limited to the shapes it needs — a `[project.optional-dependencies]` table of string arrays, including multi-line arrays, inline comments and both quote styles — and produces byte-identical metadata to the `tomllib` path; it must not add a build requirement or import a third-party TOML parser.

R6. `build_wheel(...)` writes a `METADATA` containing `Provides-Extra: test` and the pytest `Requires-Dist` line, and `build_sdist(...)` writes a `PKG-INFO` with the same extras, both from the same `_metadata()` text so the wheel and sdist cannot diverge.
R7. `prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel` writes the same `METADATA` text as the wheel, so `pip` sees the extra before building.

R8. `README.md`'s `## Tests` section shows, in a fenced block, an install line of the form `python3 -m pip install "<wheel path or git url with tag>[test]"` and then `python -m pytest -q`; it also keeps `python -m unittest discover -s tests` documented as the path that needs no installation.
R9. `README.md` contains no editable-install instruction: no `-e`, `--editable`, `pip install -e` or equivalent text; the existing sentence stating editable installs are unsupported is kept.
R10. `install.sh`, the one-command install line, the update line, the uninstall line, the Windows fallback line and the absence of a `pipx` line are unchanged.
R11. No file under `forgel_code/` is modified.

R12. New tests cover: (a) the `test` extra in `pyproject.toml` matches R1; (b) wheel `METADATA` carries `Provides-Extra: test` and the pytest `Requires-Dist` line with the `extra == "test"` marker; (c) the pytest requirement in the wheel `METADATA` equals the one declared in `pyproject.toml`; (d) sdist `PKG-INFO` carries the same two lines; (e) rewriting the extras table in a throw-away copy of the tree changes the emitted requirement, proving a single source; (f) the fallback parser produces the same result as `tomllib` for the real table; (g) an offline `pip install` of the local tree with `[test]` exits 0.

R13. `tests/test_readme_install.py` continues to forbid `pip install` outside the `## Tests` section, continues to forbid `pipx`, virtualenv recipes, `--user` outside the Windows line, and gains an assertion that no editable install appears anywhere in `README.md`.
R14. No existing test is deleted, skipped or weakened; `tests/test_packaging.py`'s `dependencies = []` assertion continues to hold against the extended `pyproject.toml`.

R15. The offline install test runs pip against the local tree with `--no-index`, `--no-build-isolation`, `--no-deps`, `--no-cache-dir` and a temporary `--target`, plus an environment that strips `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_FIND_LINKS` and sets `PIP_NO_INDEX=1`, so it cannot reach the network and cannot install pytest as a side effect.
acceptance: A1. `pyproject.toml` declares exactly one extra, `test`, containing one lower-bounded `pytest` requirement with no upper cap, and `[project] dependencies` is still `[]`.
A2. Building a wheel from the tree yields a `METADATA` containing both `Provides-Extra: test` and `Requires-Dist: pytest...; extra == "test"`.
A3. A test asserts that the pytest requirement in the wheel `METADATA` equals the requirement declared in `pyproject.toml`, so the two cannot drift.
A4. The sdist `PKG-INFO` built from the same tree carries the same `Provides-Extra` and pytest `Requires-Dist` lines as the wheel `METADATA`.
A5. Changing the pytest requirement in a copied `pyproject.toml` changes the emitted metadata accordingly, proving the backend has a single source for the extra.
A6. With `tomllib` made unavailable, the backend still emits the same `Provides-Extra`/`Requires-Dist` lines and still declares no build requirement.
A7. An offline `pip install` of the local tree with the `test` extra and `--no-deps` exits 0 without network access.

A8. `README.md` shows installing with the `test` extra followed by `python -m pytest -q`, keeps `python -m unittest discover -s tests` as the no-install path, and contains no editable-install instruction.
A9. `git status --porcelain -- forgel_code` is empty for the change: no file under `forgel_code/` is touched.
A10. `python3 -m pytest -q` exits 0 from a clean checkout; no test is deleted, skipped or weakened.
constraints: Python >=3.9 must remain installable: the backend cannot assume `tomllib` exists.
The build backend keeps `requires = []`: no setuptools, no tomli, no network access during a build.
Test runs must not require network access.
Do not weaken or remove existing tests to make the new ones pass.
Committed artifacts, commit messages and documentation are in English; commits are signed off with `-s`.
No tool attribution lines or session references in commits or pull requests.
assumptions: The extra is named `test`; no `dev` extra with linters is added, since the user asked only for test dependencies.
The pytest constraint is a lower bound (`pytest>=7`) with no upper cap, matching the request for a lower bound without a ceiling.
The single source of the extras is `pyproject.toml`; the backend derives the metadata from it rather than repeating the version.
The README's existing Tests section is the place to document the extra; the rest of the install documentation is not restructured.
The existing offline-install test style (`--no-index --no-build-isolation --no-deps` into a temporary `--target`) is the pattern for the new extras test.

external_dependencies.name: pytest
external_dependencies.interface: Run the repository test suite with `python3 -m pytest -q`; the `test` extra declares pytest with a lower-bound requirement, and the backend republishes that same requirement in wheel metadata.
external_dependencies.evidence: Repository `environment.yaml` is the build/commands/env contract; `README.md` documents the `## Tests` path; `tests/` is the local test suite; the acceptance command is `python3 -m pytest -q`.

external_dependencies.name: pip
external_dependencies.interface: Drive the real pip CLI for the offline install test: `python3 -m pip install --no-index --no-build-isolation --no-deps "<local tree>[test]"`; the build/wheel path also uses pip to exercise the local backend.
external_dependencies.evidence: `environment.yaml` supplies the local Python/pip toolchain; the repository tests invoke `python3 -m pip` directly with network-disabling and no-build-isolation flags; pip reads the backend-prepared metadata to decide whether the `test` extra exists.

external_dependencies.name: PEP 621 `[project.optional-dependencies]` and core metadata fields `Provides-Extra` / `Requires-Dist`
external_dependencies.interface: `pyproject.toml` records `[project.optional-dependencies].test`; `_build_backend.py` parses that table and emits `Provides-Extra: test` plus `Requires-Dist: pytest...; extra == "test"` into METADATA/PKG-INFO.
external_dependencies.evidence: `pyproject.toml` is the declared source for project metadata, including the empty `[project] dependencies` and the new `test` extra; `_build_backend.py` is the local metadata emitter used to build the wheel and sdist.

external_dependencies.name: TOML (and the `tomllib` module)
external_dependencies.interface: Use stdlib `tomllib.load` on Python 3.11+; on Python 3.9/3.10, use an in-tree fallback parser for the limited `[project.optional-dependencies]` table shape (`dict[str, list[str]]`) rather than adding a build dependency.
external_dependencies.evidence: `pyproject.toml` is TOML and declares `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, so Python 3.9/3.10 may lack `tomllib`; `_build_backend.py` must therefore carry the limited in-tree fallback. Python 3.11+ provides `tomllib` as a standard-library module.

external_dependencies.name: PEP 517 build-backend hooks (`prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel`, `build_wheel`, `build_sdist`)
external_dependencies.interface: pip invokes the in-tree `_build_backend.py` hooks in-process; `prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel` must advertise the `test` extra before installation, and `build_wheel`/`build_sdist` must emit consistent metadata.
external_dependencies.evidence: `pyproject.toml` uses the local build backend; `_build_backend.py` implements the wheel/sdist metadata generation; the tests build a wheel from the tree and inspect its METADATA for `Provides-Extra: test` and the pytest `Requires-Dist` line.

result.summary: Declared the `test` extra once in `pyproject.toml` (`[project.optional-dependencies] test = ["pytest>=7"]`, runtime `dependencies = []` untouched), made `_build_backend.py` derive `Provides-Extra: test` and `Requires-Dist: pytest>=7; extra == "test"` from that table so wheel METADATA, sdist PKG-INFO and `prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel` share one source, and added an in-tree TOML fallback for Python 3.9/3.10 (no `tomllib`, no new build requirement). Rewrote the README `## Tests` section to show installing a pinned revision with `[test]` and running `python -m pytest -q` while keeping `python -m unittest discover -s tests` as the no-install path. Extended `tests/test_readme_install.py` narrowly: the pip-install guard now allows exactly one `pip install` line that carries `[test]` inside the `## Tests` section, plus a new assertion forbidding any editable install, and a new `Tests` section check. Added `tests/test_extras.py` covering the declaration shape, wheel METADATA, sdist PKG-INFO, drift between pyproject and METADATA, single-source behaviour via a rewritten copy, the fallback parser versus `tomllib`, and a real offline `pip install` of the tree with `[test]`. Tested with `python3 -m pytest -q` (163 passed, 137 subtests) and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` (163 tests, OK); `git status --porcelain -- forgel_code` is empty.; final test command exited 124
